prehistory-iberia-steppe-ancestry-turnov.name: Steppe-related migration and sex-biased ancestry turnover in Iberia
prehistory-iberia-steppe-ancestry-turnov.mechanism: Migration, coexistence, admixture, and sex-biased ancestry turnover.
agents: Incoming people carrying steppe-related ancestry, associated in part with Bell Beaker networks
victims: Earlier Copper Age populations in Iberia; substantial local ancestry persisted, and no bounded displaced or victim cohort is demonstrated
prehistory-iberia-steppe-ancestry-turnov.summary: Between roughly 2500 and 2000 BCE, incoming people carrying steppe-related ancestry coexisted and admixed with local populations in Iberia. Post-2000 BCE groups derived about 40 percent of their ancestry from the incoming population, while Y-chromosome lineages common in sampled Copper Age groups nearly ceased to be observed. This supports strongly sex-biased ancestry turnover, not documented killing, expulsion, or residential displacement.
prehistory-iberia-steppe-ancestry-turnov.confidence: high on migration, admixture, approximate autosomal ancestry change, and near-complete sampled Y-chromosome lineage turnover; unknown on the social process and unsupported for a bounded coerced-displacement or victim cohort
prehistory-iberia-steppe-ancestry-turnov.post_v5_source_calibration: The cited studies do not identify a bounded displaced cohort or destination. Separation from homeland is structurally inapplicable to the demonstrated evidence rather than a supported zero.
